summary: GH gutenberg#82251 / Trac #66001 (Font Library page renders pre-auth) is genuinely fixed in 7.1.1+ — anonymous GET to admin-post.php?page=font-library and page=options-connectors both 302 to wp-login on WordPress 7.1.2
notes: Confirmed via real end-to-end HTTP render on the courtneyr.dev dev environment (7.1.2 / PHP 8.5.10) 2026-09-24 — closes the 'not executed: end-to-end HTTP render' gap the original draft flagged. Source guard (is_user_logged_in/current_user_can/auth_redirect) present in wp-includes/build/pages/font-library/page.php.

summary: A single-sweep 'N requests, 0 hits' claim was read as a durable fix for WordPress/mcp-adapter#332's per-request ability-registration-order bug; a fresh retest on the same build (7.1.2) reproduced the bug cleanly and repeatably via real REST requests
decision: method-failure — false negative from insufficient/wrong-shaped sampling
notes: 2026-09-22 comment on mcp-adapter#332 claimed 0 of the 3 [ERROR] lines over 44 requests on 7.1.2. 2026-09-24 retest: a bare wp-cli 'wp eval' reproduced it 0/6 times, but a real anonymous REST GET (/wp-json/wp/v2/posts) reproduced all 3 lines cleanly on 3/3 separate attempts, and 2 more bursts appeared during exploratory wp-cli calls whose bodies happened to load extra plugin classes. The trigger is tied to the rest_api_init bootstrap path (mcp-adapter hooks it at priority 15), which most bare CLI evals never exercise. Read via SFTP pull of logs/php/php-error.log (before/after diff), not wp debug.log (WP_DEBUG_LOG is off on this site).

summary: dshanske/simple-location#298 (rest_prepare_post date_gmt/modified_gmt without isset) still reproduces unchanged on 7.1.2 / Simple Location 5.0.25
notes: Same REST request that retested FM-36 reproduced 12 warnings (4 per post x 3 posts) at includes/class-loc-timezone.php:81/82/83/85. Reliable single-shot repro; good calibration case for 'REST _fields warning' detectors.

summary: Trac tickets ARE readable this cycle through the hosted wordpress-trac MCP tool (courtneyr-dev/meta-trac) — it answered #66001 and #65489 in full (description + comments + linked PRs + changesets) with no 403

notes: Keep as a negative control for any rewrite-flush detector: an upgrade cell that requests /random/ before any admin request will see a 404 that is not a defect.

notes: Without the header-mismatch control, a pass on old libzip only proves the happy path. The control is built by extension-install-suite.sh.

summary: Fixtures auto-updated core mid-party: a multisite fixture moved from the Beta 5 package to nightly 7.2-beta5-65392 at 12:21 local, so its subsite media run (47 PASS) was on the nightly, not the package under test
notes: Found only by reading $wp_version after the batch. WP_AUTO_UPDATE_CORE false then set on 10 fixtures; beta-tester auto-update fixtures left as they were on purpose.

summary: Browser-sweep harness traps: welcome guides, the new-page pattern chooser, hidden duplicate Save buttons, quoted CSV in an assertion, sticky posts defeating posts_per_page=1, WP-CLI reading --path=/site/ as its global flag, and a seed consumed by an earlier run. 7 of 14 T2 cells failed identically on 7.2-beta5 and 7.1.4; after fixing the harness all 28 passed
notes: Identical failure on the target and the prior-stable control was the tell every time. No product defect behind any of them.

summary: X-SERIAL-01 block fixed-point: an empty object attribute {"color":{}} round-trips to [] (Theme Unit Test post "WP 6.1 Media category blocks"); same on 7.1.4
notes: Exclude this post, or normalize empty {} vs [], before any byte-diff assertion, or every re-save diff reports it.

summary: Turning random content redirects off with wp_enable_random_content_redirect leaves the stored /random/ rule in place: /random/ serves a copy of the home page with HTTP 200 until rewrite rules are flushed; a wp-admin request does not flush them (7.2-beta5)
decision: DOCUMENTED (the filter docblock says to flush)
notes: A fleet note, not a ticket. CaptainCore flushes once per WordPress version after disabling it (captaincore 6516f106, 2026-11-09).

notes: Seen in the upstream-watch review on 2026-11-10; affects step 3 imports of fleet probe results.

summary: Installing a 7.0.x or older ladder source with wp core download (a tar.gz) cuts paths longer than 100 characters, so the stale-file check reports leftovers that were never in the package (21 php-ai-client files on 7.0.8, cut at 90 of 105 characters).
notes: 7.0.8 from the zip through the Core updater leaves 0 stale files. The sweep playbook already names the tar trap; this adds the register row and the control. Seen in the 7.2 RC1 and RC3 ladders.

notes: The 7.1.4 to 7.1.5 pair, run by hand, gave 21 patched and 0 VULNERABLE on RC3 and 17 VULNERABLE on RC1.

notes: Rerun in sequence, the same RC1 run reported 17 VULNERABLE.

notes: Found in the 7.2 RC3 chain lanes; the thin-content results were kept apart from the valid rerun.

summary: zsh does not word-split an unquoted variable, so set -- $var in a helper leaves the whole string in $1. A sub-size check and a stale-file loop judged a 6-size pass as a FAIL.
notes: The Bash tool shell here is zsh.

summary: A behavior probe that reads the same on the pre-fix build and on the fixed build measures nothing. A case-variant note comment was readable by an anonymous REST request on 7.1.3, 7.1.5 and RC3 alike, because the 7.1.4 hardening sits in the edit permission, not the read path.
notes: No attacker boundary shown; kept as a probe that does not separate builds.

notes: Seen with Chrome for Testing 151 through Playwright 1.57.

summary: A prior-stable copy made by replacing a newer site's files keeps the newer db_version, so every admin page redirects to upgrade.php and every browser cell fails on both builds.
